```{r}
roc_list <- prebs %>%
  group_split(eco_split) %>%
  map(~ {
    roc_obj <- roc(.x$progression, .x$prediction_prob, quiet = TRUE)
    data.frame(
      specificity = rev(roc_obj$specificities),
      sensitivity = rev(roc_obj$sensitivities),
      eco_split = unique(.x$eco_split)
    )
  }) %>%
  bind_rows()

# Calculate AUC values for each subset
auc_labels <- prebs %>%
  group_split(eco_split) %>%
  map_df(~ {
    roc_obj <- roc(.x$progression, .x$prediction_prob, quiet = TRUE)
    data.frame(eco_split = unique(.x$eco_split), auc = as.numeric(auc(roc_obj)))
  })

# Plot with ggplot2
roc_plot <- ggplot(roc_list, aes(x = 1 - specificity, y = sensitivity, color = eco_split)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  labs(
    x = "1 - Specificity (False Positive Rate)",
    y = "Sensitivity (True Positive Rate)"
  ) +
  theme_light(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",  # Remove the legend
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),  # Increase axis title text size
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12)     # Increase axis text size
  )

# Add AUC annotations to the plot
for (i in seq_along(auc_labels$eco_split)) {
  roc_plot <- roc_plot +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = 0.6,
      y = 0.4 - 0.1 * i,
      label = paste(auc_labels$eco_split[i], "set AUC:", round(auc_labels$auc[i], 3)),
      color = "black",
      size = 6
    )
}

# Print the plot
print(roc_plot)

ggsave(file.path(parent_folder,"fig_plot","eco_model_roc.pdf"), roc_plot, width = 14, height = 9, dpi = 300, units = "cm")
```

```{r}

plot_save_cm <- function(results,eco_split = FALSE){
    
  results_data <- filter(results, risk_category != "Diploid")
  if (eco_split != FALSE){
    results_data <- results_data %>%
      filter(eco_split == !!eco_split)
  }
  results_data$predicted_binary <- ifelse(results_data$risk_category == "High Risk", 1, 0)
  
  # Create mapping for actual outcomes
  # progression: 1 -> Progression, 0 -> Non-Progression  
  results_data$actual_binary <- results_data$progression
  
  # Create labels for plotting
  results_data$predicted_label <- ifelse(results_data$predicted_binary == 1, "CO", "NCO")
  results_data$actual_label <- ifelse(results_data$progression == 1, "CO", "NCO")
  
  # Create confusion matrix using table
  cm_table <- table(Actual = results_data$actual_label, 
                    Predicted = results_data$predicted_label)
  
  # Convert to data frame
  confusion_matrix <- data.frame(
    Actual = rownames(cm_table),
    CO = cm_table[, "CO"],
    NCO = cm_table[, "NCO"]
  )
  
  # Calculate the total for each actual class
  confusion_matrix$Total <- rowSums(confusion_matrix[, -1])
  
  # Calculate percentages
  confusion_matrix_percent <- confusion_matrix
  confusion_matrix_percent[, 2:3] <- confusion_matrix[, 2:3] / confusion_matrix$Total * 100
  
  # Melt the data frame for percentages
  confusion_matrix_melted_percent <- melt(select(confusion_matrix_percent, -Total),
                                          id.vars = "Actual",
                                          variable.name = "Predicted",
                                          value.name = "Percentage")
  
  # Melt the data frame for absolute numbers
  confusion_matrix_melted_abs <- melt(select(confusion_matrix, -Total),
                                      id.vars = "Actual",
                                      variable.name = "Predicted",
                                      value.name = "Count")
  
  # Clean up the predicted column names (remove underscores and make proper labels)
  confusion_matrix_melted_percent$Predicted <- gsub("_", " ", confusion_matrix_melted_percent$Predicted)
  confusion_matrix_melted_abs$Predicted <- gsub("_", " ", confusion_matrix_melted_abs$Predicted)
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = confusion_matrix_melted_percent,
              aes(y = Actual, x = Predicted, fill = Percentage)) +
    geom_text(data = confusion_matrix_melted_percent,
              aes(y = Actual, x = Predicted, label = paste0(round(Percentage, 1), "%")),
              color = "black", size = 7, vjust = -0.5) +
    geom_text(data = confusion_matrix_melted_abs,
              aes(y = Actual, x = Predicted, label = Count),
              color = "black", size = 6, vjust = 1.5) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "darkgreen") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
    labs(x = "Predicted", y = "Actual") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
          legend.position = "none",
          axis.title = element_text(size = 16)) 
  
  p
  filename <- ifelse(eco_split == FALSE, 
                     "cm_eco.pdf", 
                     paste0("cm_eco_", eco_split, ".pdf"))
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(parent_folder, "fig_plot", filename),
    plot = p, 
    width = 10, 
    height = 9, 
    dpi = 300, 
    units = "cm"
  )
  return(p)
}
plot_save_cm(results)
plot_save_cm(results,"train")
plot_save_cm(results,"val")
```

```{r}
ggsave_workaround <- function(g){survminer:::.build_ggsurvplot(x = g,
                                                               surv.plot.height = NULL,
                                                               risk.table.height = NULL,
                                                               ncensor.plot.height = NULL)}

create_survival_plot <- function(data, color_set = 1, dataset_name, group_var, title_suffix = "") {
  # Create formula object directly
  data <- data%>%filter(fu_time > 14)
  formula_obj <- as.formula(paste("Surv(fu_time/365, progression) ~", group_var))

  # Create survival fit
  fit <- surv_fit(formula_obj, data = data)
  
  # Create plot title
  plot_title <- paste("Survival Curve -", dataset_name, title_suffix)
  
colors <- NULL
tables.height <- NULL

# Switch statement to set colors and tables.height based on color_set
switch(color_set,
       `1` = {
         colors <- c("#4575b4", "#fc8d59")
         tables.height <- 0.3
       },
       `2` = {
         colors <- c("#fee090", "#fc8d59")
         tables.height <- 0.3
       },
       `3` = {
         colors <- c("#2c7bb6", "#fee090", "#d7191c")
         tables.height <- 0.35  
       },
       {
         stop("Invalid color_set value. Please use 1, 2, or 3.")
       }
)

  # Create survival plot - let ggsurvplot calculate p-value internally
  plot <- ggsurvplot(fit, 
                  data = data,
                  pval = TRUE,
                  # title = plot_title,
                  xlab = "Time (years)",
                  risk.table = T, 
                  conf.int = FALSE,
                  palette = colors,
                  legend = "none",
                  risk.table.y.text = FALSE,
                  tables.height = tables.height,
                  # Text sizing with Arial font
                  font.main = c(18, "bold"),      # Main title
                  font.x = c(10, "bold"),         # X-axis title
                  font.y = c(8, "bold"),         # Y-axis title  
                  font.tickslab = c(12, "plain"), # Axis tick labels
                  font.legend = c(14, "bold"),    # Legend text
                  pval.size = 5,                           # P-value text size
                  size = 1,                              # Survival curve line thickness
                  # Risk table styling
                  risk.table.fontsize = 4,
                  ggtheme = theme_survminer() + 
                    theme(axis.line = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
                          axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
                          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)))
  
  
  # Print the plot
 print(plot)
  
  p <- ggsave_workaround(plot)
  return(p)
}

```
